as_written_in_papers.quote: Adult-Onset Alexander Disease With c.619 G>A Mutation

cases.statement: One person: a 76-year-old man with very-late-onset mild pyramidal signs, autopsy-confirmed Rosenthal fibres.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: mild spastic gait, bilateral Babinski, increased deep tendon reflexes at 76; ventral medulla T2 hyperintensity and marked spinal cord atrophy; widespread Rosenthal fibres at autopsy; left cranial nerve III/IV/VI palsy attributed to an orbital schwannoma

quotes.quote: A 76-year-old man with neither medical history nor family history of neurologic diseases presented with progressive diplopia and ptosis in his left eye.
Mild spastic gait with bilateral positive Babinski reflex and increased deep tendon reflex in all limbs was observed.

Unexpectedly, brain and spinal MRI revealed bilateral abnormal high intensities in the ventral medulla oblongata, a mild periventricular hyperintensity lesion, and marked spinal cord atrophy (Figure, A and B).
These findings are characteristic of adult-onset ALXDRD,^1 and Sanger sequencing analysis of GFAP disclosed a novel heterozygous c.619-1G>A mutation.

Fibrotic astrocyte degeneration, Rosenthal fiber deposition, and myelin loss were widespread in the medulla, spinal cord, and periventricular locations underlying the lateral ventricles and fourth ventricle (Figure C), which was pathologically compatible with ALXDRD.^4

phenotype_specificity.statement: Autopsy showed widespread Rosenthal fibres, judged pathologically compatible with AxD; MRI pattern described as characteristic. The ocular palsies were attributed to an orbital schwannoma (GFAP-negative), and the patient had metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma. No testing of other genes is described.

quotes.quote: Fibrotic astrocyte degeneration, Rosenthal fiber deposition, and myelin loss were widespread in the medulla, spinal cord, and periventricular locations underlying the lateral ventricles and fourth ventricle (Figure C), which was pathologically compatible with ALXDRD.^4

The orbital lesion was schwannoma, which was confirmed by the typical palisading with positive S-100 staining and negative GFAP staining immunohistochemistry and considered not to be related to ALXDRD.
In addition, systemic screening revealed gastric adenocarcinoma with multiple metastases in para-aortic lymph nodes.

segregation.statement: No relatives tested; no family history of neurologic disease.

quotes.quote: A 76-year-old man with neither medical history nor family history of neurologic diseases presented with progressive diplopia and ptosis in his left eye.

functional.statement: Patient tissue (autopsy brain RNA): RT-PCR products cloned; 20 of 54 clones carried r.619_621del (GAG deletion) from use of a cryptic acceptor 2-3 nt into exon 4, predicted p.Glu207del; exon 4 skipping, which the authors expected, was not reported. No control tissue is described.

quotes.quote: However, analysis of RNA from the autopsied brain tissue of the present patient showed deletion of GAG (r.619_621del) (Figure D).
The number of wild-type and mutant clones was 34 and 20, respectively.

These findings suggested that c.619-1G>A caused activation of the cryptic splice acceptor site in the second and third nucleotides from the 5′ end of exon 4 (Figure D), in approximately 37% (20/54) of the transcripts.
Because c.619-1G>A is located in the canonical splice acceptor site of intron 3, we initially expected that this mutation would result in exon 4 skipping.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Canonical splice acceptor change (intron 3, -1). RNA evidence in the paper shows an in-frame 3-nt loss, p.Glu207del, in the 1B helical segment; the authors reason from missense changes at Glu207 reported in AxD.

quotes.quote: r.619_621del results in loss of Glu207, which is located in the α-helical segment 1B.
Loss of Glu207 is believed to be pathogenic because the missense mutations at Glu207, p.Glu207Gln,^5 p.Glu207Lys,^6 and p.Glu207Val^7 have been previously reported in patients with ALXDRD.

authors_classification.statement: Authors call it a novel disease-causing mutation; no ACMG criteria stated.

quotes.quote: In conclusion, we identified a novel ALXDRD-causing GFAP mutation in the splice acceptor site of intron 3, leading to activation of a cryptic splice site in exon 4.

concerns: Protein differs from the batch prediction: the paper gives p.Glu207del from brain RNA, while the predicted protein from the cDNA is p.?; the RNA result supports an in-frame deletion rather than skipping.
Figure title writes 'c.619 G>A' (missing '-1'), inconsistent with c.619-1G>A elsewhere in the paper.
Transcript not stated in the paper.
Concurrent metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma and an orbital schwannoma; the ocular palsies are attributed to the schwannoma.
No parental or family testing; very late onset (76 years).
notes_for_panel: Autopsy-confirmed case (Rosenthal fibres) with patient-tissue RNA evidence of aberrant splicing in about 37% of transcripts.
